reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the plan still needed revising in the last round (round 3 of 3). I read reading.rs (is_bullet and request_text_acceptance at 1992-2008, check_reading_acceptance at 2599, check_governance_coverage at 2674) and briefs.rs (READING_RULES at 1557, the rule-section test at 3172). The plan fixes the right place. check_reading_acceptance is the gate every reading passes, and the plan's call site, early return and refusal message follow check_governance_coverage. Its demonstrations call the real gate and use the existing scoped_reading helper. The briefs.rs change fits the rule-section test: one more line of about 190 bytes keeps the section under its 2400-byte cap, by my estimate, not a measurement. I found two soundness problems. First, the parser checks only `(N)` markers and Acceptance bullets. That drops the `N.` and `N)` numbered parts the accepted reading designed for, so a plain numbered request still lets the reader defer a part. Second, the stem rules as specified do not let a typical criterion cover the standard Steward bullet 'A test fails without the change…'. The stop list is applied in an unstated order, 'without' is not in it, and two shared stems are required. This contradicts the plan's own Criterion 6 hand-check and puts false refusals on the most common request shape. Also minor: an affirmative pattern inside a quoted complaint still exempts the part. Both major findings can be fixed inside the plan, so the verdict is revise. Findings: major: The plan drops the `N)` and `N.` part forms the accepted reading designed for, so a plain numbered list of parts is never checked. (Plan Decision 2 (parts parser) vs. the accepted reading's Design assumption); major: Applied as written, the plan's stem rules do not let a typical criterion cover the standard Steward bullet, which contradicts the plan's own demonstration and points to false refusals on every Steward request. (Plan Decision 3 (stems / stop list) and the Criterion 6 demonstration (ii), Steward-bullet hand-check); minor: An affirmative pattern inside a quoted or reported sentence still exempts the part. (Plan Decision 5 (affirmative exemption)); nit: Criterion 1 says the test uses the 'real request text' of job 20261029-084645-sza7, but the plan rebuilds it from the brief. (Plan Demonstration for Criterion 1)
